key_insight: PRIMS embeds fluid physics directly into a multimodal Transformer, making fluid identification more accurate, interpretable, and robust to changing operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable on-device microfluidic sensing for real-world systems where flow, pressure, and temperature vary continuously.
method: Physics-based Token Vectorization converts Coriolis and pressure signals into physically meaningful embeddings.
Physical Component Synthesizer captures viscosity-related links among flow, pressure, and density.
Physics-guided Fusion uses attention to combine cross-physical signals in a physics-aware way.
evidence_signal: On a five-fluid benchmark with dynamic flow, pressure, and temperature, PRIMS achieved 98.92% average F1-score with only 0.46M parameters and showed strong out-of-distribution robustness.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate sensor calibration and on how well the embedded physics assumptions match the target microfluidic setup.
paper_title: PRIMS: Physics-guided Representation for Fluid Identification in Multimodal Sensing
